newsitem.title: BRUNEI: Mandela calls for African-ASEAN links.
newsitem.headline: Mandela calls for African-ASEAN links.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Tuesday called for closer links between the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and a southern African trade grouping.
Speaking at a banquet hosted by Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, Mandela said Southeast Asian countries ranked among the top trading and investment partners in southern Africa.
ASEAN, which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, seeks to create a regional free trade area by 2003.

"In this context, we look forward to closer cooperation between ASEAN and our own regional organisation, the Southern African Development Community (SADC), as a development that can only bode well for the 600 million inhabitants of these two regional blocs," Mandela said. He did not elaborate.

Mandela, accompanied by his companion Graca Machel, 51, the widow of Mozambique's founding president, Samora Machel, arrived in Brunei on Monday from the Philippines on a 10-day, four-nation tour of Southeast Asia.
Machel is accompanying Mandela for the first time on a state visit.

South Africa's Deputy Trade Minister Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka told reporters Mandela had asked the Sultan to resume oil exports to South Africa to revive trade that had dwindled to almost nothing during Pretoria's apartheid regime.
She said South Africa also welcomed Brunei investments.
The tiny sultanate on Borneo island has built an investment portfolio estimated at between $30 billion and $60 billion from its petroleum revenues.
Earlier on Tuesday, Mandela took a boat ride around a village built over the Brunei river, occasionally hopping on to boardwalks to greet startled residents.

Mandela shook hands with women in full Islamic attire who are unaccustomed to touching men in public, kissed delighted children and hugged the village chieftain on his tour of Kampong Air, or "water village".

Around half of the residents of Brunei's capital of Bandar Seri Begawan live in the village, a sprawling patchwork of houses, schools, clinics and shops all built on stilts over the river and connected by a maze of boardwalks.
Mandela leaves for Singapore on Wednesday and visits Malaysia the following day.
